prompt: Detect a suspected infinite loop from the line numbers a program keeps re-executing. Complete LoopCycleDetector, then run the tests.
explanation: A block of length k repeats three times at the tail exactly when every entry in the last 3*k equals the entry k positions later -- comparing the first 2*k of them against their partners checks both repetitions in one loop. Trying k in increasing order and returning immediately is what satisfies the "smallest k" rule: {3,3,3,3,3,3} is a repeat at k=1 and k=2, and the loop finds k=1 first. Capping k at length/3 is both the correctness rule and the reason a short trace simply returns an empty list instead of reading past the end of the array.
hints: Loop k from 1 up to executed.length / 3 and return as soon as one k works -- that gives you the smallest k for free.
For a given k, the tail starts at index length - 3*k; the block repeats when executed[i] == executed[i + k] for every i in the first 2*k positions of that tail.
The k loop simply does not run when the array is shorter than 3 entries, so the empty-trace case needs no special handling.
